## Trial `password-complexity-policy-ubunt__xjVPVpv`

**Verifier decision: Full Success.** The executor correctly installed libpam-pwquality and set minlen=12/minclass=3 in pwquality.conf on node1, and directly demonstrated enforcement via live passwd attempts as an unprivileged user: passwords under 12 characters were rejected, passwords with fewer than 3 character classes were rejected, and a compliant password was accepted. This was verified both before and after a full node restart (boot_id changed from f9bf293d... to 902575df..., matching the fixed global snapshots), confirming the policy persists across reboot. Temporary test users were cleaned up and no unnecessary or unexplained mutations were found; the environment returned to a clean state.

| Reward | Coverage | Functionality | Hygiene | Confidence | Commands |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 0.950 | 0.930 | 14/4 (+1 dropped) |

### Why the verifier reached this decision

- **req-minlen — Satisfied:** New user passwords on node1 must be at least 12 characters long
  - **Why:** libpam-pwquality installed, minlen=12 added to /etc/security/pwquality.conf, and a live passwd attempt by an unprivileged user with a password under 12 characters was rejected with an explicit 'password is shorter than 12 characters' message both before and after the node restart, while a compliant longer password was accepted.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-2dadaf74142f4725`, `cmd-53159c779af14359`, `cmd-0ddab7242d9f4e8c`, `cmd-b89ff45281064c57`, `cmd-12af0b121d794e24`, `cmd-be4b1eaa1b55490a`
- **req-minclass — Satisfied:** New user passwords on node1 must use at least three different character classes
  - **Why:** minclass=3 added to pwquality.conf; a live passwd attempt with a lowercase-only password was rejected with 'password contains less than 3 character classes', while a 4-class password was accepted, both before and after the restart.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-2dadaf74142f4725`, `cmd-4b829fa001e44d16`, `cmd-b89ff45281064c57`, `cmd-12af0b121d794e24`, `cmd-be4b1eaa1b55490a`
- **req-pam-wiring — Satisfied:** Policy must actually be enforced via PAM on new password changes (not just present in a config file)
  - **Why:** grep confirms pam_pwquality.so is wired into /etc/pam.d/common-password (via requisite), and functional passwd tests as an unprivileged user demonstrate the policy is enforced end-to-end, not merely configured.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-a2c74f1d6d434c88`, `cmd-53159c779af14359`, `cmd-4b829fa001e44d16`, `cmd-b89ff45281064c57`

### Operational hygiene

The verifier assigned hygiene **0.950**. All state-changing commands map cleanly to the task: package install, config append, and two rounds of temporary test-user creation/passwd-testing/deletion (pre- and post-restart) to validate the policy live. Both test users (pwtestuser, pwverify) were deleted after use; userdel returned rc=1 only due to a harmless 'mail spool not found' warning, with 'id' confirming the users no longer exist. No abandoned files, failed services, or unnecessary mutations were found — after_executor snapshot shows only expected reboot-driven differences (new boot_id, new /tmp systemd-private dirs, listening sockets re-bound to a new resolver pid), all matching a normal reboot, not executor residue. The restart itself (shutdown -r now) was a required action for the mandatory node-restart evidence protocol.
